title: Baseline Is Not Health
subtitle: Epistemic baselines, intervention epochs, and the danger of teaching condition-monitoring systems that the first stable state is a healthy state
rights: Copyright Mark Yarian. All rights reserved; public reading and citation permitted.
abstract: Condition-monitoring systems commonly compare current measurements with baselines, thresholds, learned distributions, or reference windows. This paper argues that a stable initial distribution is evidence of repeatability, not evidence of health, and proposes explicit separation between observed and health-validated baselines together with intervention-bounded temporal epochs. Maintenance events become evidence-bearing boundaries for pre/post comparison without automatic causal attribution. The architecture preserves provenance, timing uncertainty, operating context, and historical baselines so later evidence can reinterpret earlier stable states without rewriting history.
evidence_classification: Conceptual architecture and proposed baseline/maintenance evaluation; no measured diagnostic improvement.
